dependency_adapters.native: Definition/PdError: prototype/code/message/cause separation, native stacks and typed constructors for all 12 formatted templates. This is an adapter for errno.go definitions and errs.go type assertions, not a claim to port the external errors library or Go arbitrary printf/reflection. Private Definition fields prevent constructing a second apparent singleton from equal text/code. Clone corresponds to copying a Go error interface, not copying the pointed-to struct. Rust Display adapts %v; f64 formatting preserves signed zero, infinities, NaN and source precision. All existing keyspace-ID callers supply uint32.

ErrorField carries key=error and borrowed/owned error identity; None is Skip. Native logger/stack representation is retained. Go oracle compares basic field values; Go stack-frame text, ErrorVerbose formatting and complete zap encoder are external dependency behavior, not new logging policy.

Immutable private-field definitions are handles to the named source prototypes. Source consumers do not reassign these globals. Native enum envelope retains the typed owner in source(), while classifiers see through only this native envelope. No message-based error-code selection.

integration_decision.remove: Error::CircuitBreakerOpen and duplicate TSO EOF/count diagnostics
integration_decision.migrate: All three circuitbreaker rejection sites, their tests/region-cache assertion, native run_tso EOF and allocate_timestamps count failure. New Error::Pd and PdResourceGroup envelopes retain both concrete owner and cause. No partial grpcutil implementation is activated.
integration_decision.open: TSO pending-request error delivery/cancellation, root discovery and physical-RPC interceptor/connection lifecycle are parent-package work; existing behavior is not accepted by these three producer migrations.

compatibility: Rust Error::CircuitBreakerOpen is replaced by Error::Pd(ERR_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_OPEN); code comparisons use the shared definition. Display now includes the source PD code. TSO EOF/count diagnostics follow Go. Normal request/connection/retry/TSO scheduling is unchanged. No new dependency or worker.
